availableCommands.name: compact

availableCommands.name: context

availableCommands.name: status

availableCommands.name: config

availableCommands.name: code
availableCommands.description: Use this skill when presented with a coding task.

availableCommands.name: code-analyzing
availableCommands.description: Use to find and search code symbols, definitions, references, usage, and impact. Also use early in a session to find the project types and how to build, test, or format them.

availableCommands.name: code-commit
availableCommands.description: Use when the user says "commit", "save changes", or "check in", and after each step that works. Use this skill, not raw git commands.

availableCommands.name: code-debugging
availableCommands.description: Use when a test fails, a build fails, or the code does not do what it must do. Find the root cause before you change code.

availableCommands.name: code-map
availableCommands.description: Use when the user says "map", "architecture", or "overview", or wants the structure of the codebase. Writes ARCHITECTURE.md with Mermaid diagrams.

availableCommands.name: code-tdd
availableCommands.description: Use before you write code for a feature, a bug fix, a refactor, or a change of behavior. Write a test that fails, then write the code that makes it pass.

availableCommands.name: code-test
availableCommands.description: Use when the user wants to run tests, or after a code change. Takes a scope (named tests, unit, integration, or project), or finds the scope from the change. Runs the tests and analyzes the results.

availableCommands.name: kanban
availableCommands.description: Use to read or change the kanban board with the `tools.kanban` tool, for example to add, find, assign, move, or update a task. Tells how to use the tool.
